VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: Checked empty G (construction yields Dirichlet‑like f, nowhere continuous, vacuously satisfies continuity at no points), full G=ℝ (f≡0, continuous everywhere), single‑point Gδ via shrinking intervals (continuity only at the point), index starting at 0 (n(x) can be 0, but reciprocal uses n(x)+1≥1 so no division by zero). The decreasing property and strict increase of ι on ℕ≥1 guarantee 1/ι(n(y)+1) < 1/ι(m) when n(y)+1 > m. Density of rationals and irrationals supplies the y needed for the discontinuity argument without choice. No interval endpoints or one‑sided limits appear; all existential choices are explicit (minimum over ℕ, density used only as “every neighbourhood meets the set”).
